title: A mission that takes its work from a backlog and has none says so in Needs you, with how long; owner-work missions are not idle
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (the module comment's alert list, `Monitor`, the reading done every `check_ms`: `read_budgets` and its neighbours, `task_record`, `mission_record`, `apply_mission`, how open alerts are read back after a restart: `seed_*`), web/src/home.ts (`needsYou`, `alertTitle` and its titles by kind) and web/src/components/home/Home.tsx (the Missions card's "No mission has work open"), and docs/fleet-architecture.md (the alert list).

The problem. On the live fleet:
- Mission 4 (Spawn RSI) had no task in work for 32.5 h from 2026-11-08 23:04Z to 11-10 07:35Z, then for 3.3 h, 1.7 h and 1 h on 11-11, and has had none since 15:15Z.
- Mission 6 (Supply PA) has had none since 11-10 19:29Z, 20 h, with its 108 objectives solved and none open.
- The fleet was idle 40 minutes after it got objectives 056 and 057 (lead-mac, sync/queue.md 23:35).
Home says only "No mission has work open": no alert, nothing in Needs you, no time since, no mission named as the one waiting for its next objectives. An idle fleet is the most expensive state the owner has. Meanwhile the scorecard's "Idle hours by mission" flags the two owner-work missions (#7 75%, #8 76%) as idle beside #4 (37%) and #6 (40%), though owner work has no backlog of its own: no task there is no fault.

Required behaviour.
(a) A new alert, `mission_idle`, subject `mission #<id>`, key `mission_idle:<id>:<event>`. It fires once when a mission meets all of these, for `SPAWN_ALERT_MISSION_IDLE_SECS` (default 900; 0 disables it):
- it is not closed;
- it takes its work from an objective backlog (configured with `--backlog`/`--resident`, `objectives` on its record);
- it has had no task in work (assigned, delivered, reported, sent back, gated, landing or held) since its last task ended (landed, accepted or cancelled).
Its evidence names `mission`, `since_ms` (when that last task ended) and `event_id` (that record). Its text names the mission and says how long it has been without work. The alert step reads it at its reading (every `check_ms`), as it reads the host and the budgets.
(b) It clears at the mission's next `task.assigned` (`cleared_evidence.event_id` that record), or when the mission closes. A loop restart reads an open one back and neither fires it again nor loses it.
(c) No `mission_idle` for an owner-work mission (no objective backlog), a closed mission, or a mission with a task in work.
(d) Home: Needs you shows it as one item naming the mission (`#<id>`). The Missions card's "No mission has work open" says, for each idle backlog mission, how long it has been without work.
(e) docs/fleet-architecture.md's alert list says (a) to (c).

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/058.sh. A real `spawn loop` (alert step every 2 s, `SPAWN_ALERT_MISSION_IDLE_SECS=8`) and `spawn serve` run on a scratch database. Missions 1-3 take their work from a backlog; mission 4 is owner work. Tasks are assigned through `spawn_control_record` and cancelled with `spawn task cancel`, and mission 2 is closed with `spawn mission close`. Its checks read `GET /api/alerts` and web/src/home.ts's `needsYou` under node:
- (1) Mission 1's last task is cancelled, giving one open `mission_idle` with evidence `mission` 1, `event_id` the cancel and `since_ms` its time, its text naming mission #1.
- (2) Read once (1) has fired, which is the barrier: none for mission 3 (task delivered), mission 2 (closed), or mission 4 (owner work, without a task longer than mission 1).
- (3) Needs you shows one item naming #1.
- (4) Task 4 is assigned to mission 1, and the alert clears with `event_id` that record.
It fails with 1 on 73e3596d: no `mission_idle` exists.

The product reason. Every hour the fleet waits for objectives nobody knows it lacks is lost throughput, and the owner learns it only by opening Home and reading one gray line. Saying it in Needs you, with how long, turns an idle fleet into an action. Leaving owner work out keeps it a signal and not noise.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/, web/test/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour: alerts.rs unit tests for (a) to (c), including a restart and the default and disabled bound, and a web/test test for the Missions card's words.
